_doc: Hints for tools/disasm.py.  Addresses are 'BB:AAAA' CPU addresses.
fastrom: label banks $80-$9F instead of $00-$1F (the game runs in $00-$1F).
entry_points: [{addr, m: 8|16, x: 8|16, db?}] extra code entry points.
labels: {addr: name} names for labels (otherwise sub_/loc_/data_/tbl_/ptrs_ + address).
comments: {addr: text} comment lines emitted above the address.
data: [{start, end}] inclusive ranges that are never code.
not_code: [addr] addresses the 'unreferenced routine' heuristic must not decode.
force_code: [addr] decode even if the opcode looks suspicious (BRK/COP/WDM/STP) or the hint says data.
mx_overrides: {addr: {m?, x?, db?}} force M/X (and DB) when decoding reaches addr.
call_returns: {routine: {m?, x?}} M/X widths the routine returns with (default: unchanged / auto-inferred).
noreturn: [routine] calls to these routines do not return.
inline_tables: {routine: {entry: word|long, count?, m?, x?}} routine pops its return address and dispatches through a table placed right after the call.
jump_tables: [{addr, count}] fixes the length of a jump table (auto-detected tables stop at the first implausible entry).
no_auto_table: [addr] do not treat a table at addr as a jump table.
pointer_args: {routine: {reg: x|y, bank}} routine takes a ROM pointer in X/Y (immediates loaded at call sites become labels).

comments.00:B2F3:
sub_00B2F3, sub_00B346, sub_00B39F: never executed in the CDL traces (found
by the unreferenced-routine heuristic).  Each compares the d-pad bits of the
joypads ($20/$22 & $0F00) with a 3-entry sequence and then checks a button:
probably button-code checks.  DB is assumed to be $05, the game's usual data
bank (hint): the sequences are then d-pad masks at $05:86D3/86D9/86DF.
